title: Ephesians Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ephesians chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ephesians Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ephesians Chapter 1.

questions.question: In Ephesians 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
Blessed be the God and Father
questions.correctAnswer: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: This appears first as Paul introduces himself in Ephesians 1:1.

questions.question: Who is the author of the letter to the Ephesians?
questions.explanation: Paul identifies himself as the author in Ephesians 1:1.

questions.question: To whom is Paul writing in Ephesians 1?
questions.explanation: Paul addresses the saints which are at Ephesus in Ephesians 1:1.

questions.question: What does Paul wish for the Ephesians in Ephesians 1:2?
questions.explanation: Paul expresses his wish for grace and peace in Ephesians 1:2.

questions.question: Who has blessed us with all spiritual blessings?
options: God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ephesians 1:3.

questions.question: What are we chosen to be before Him?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:4 states we should be holy and without blame before Him.

questions.question: What has God predestinated us to?
questions.explanation: This is mentioned in Ephesians 1:5.

questions.question: What does Paul say we have through His blood?
questions.explanation: According to Ephesians 1:7, we have redemption through His blood.

questions.question: What has God abounded toward us in?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Ephesians 1:8.

questions.question: What is included in the greeting in Ephesians 1:2?
questions.explanation: Paul greets them with grace in Ephesians 1:2.

questions.question: Who is the beloved mentioned in Ephesians 1:6?
questions.explanation: The beloved refers to Jesus Christ in the context of Ephesians 1:6.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was an apostle by the will of God.
questions.explanation: Paul states he is an apostle by the will of God in Ephesians 1:1.

questions.question: True or False: We have forgiveness of sins according to the riches of His grace.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:7 states we have forgiveness of sins according to the riches of His grace.

questions.question: True or False: Paul wrote to the believers in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Paul is writing to the saints in Ephesus, not Jerusalem, as stated in Ephesians 1:1.

questions.question: True or False: Ephesians 1 states that we are chosen for worldly riches.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1 focuses on spiritual blessings and holiness, not worldly riches, as stated in Ephesians 1:3 and 1:4.

medium.title: Ephesians Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ephesians Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 1:9, what has been made known to us?
options: The prophecies of the end times
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:9 states, 'Having made known unto us the mystery of his will...' which is the correct answer.

questions.question: What will happen if we trust in Christ, as stated in Ephesians 1:12?
options: We should be to the praise of his glory
We will live a long life
questions.correctAnswer: We should be to the praise of his glory
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:12 says, 'That we should be to the praise of his glory, who first trusted in Christ,' indicating the outcome of trusting in Christ.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the inheritance we have obtained according to Ephesians 1:11?
options: Being predestinated according to his purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Being predestinated according to his purpose
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:11 states, 'In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him...' which supports the correct answer.

questions.question: What connection is made between hearing the word of truth and being sealed, as per Ephesians 1:13?
options: Hearing leads to being sealed with the holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Hearing leads to being sealed with the holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:13 states, 'In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth... ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,' showing the direct connection.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 1:14, what is the holy Spirit described as?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:14 describes the holy Spirit as 'Which is the earnest of our inheritance until the redemption of the purchased possession...' confirming the correct answer.

questions.question: How does Paul respond to hearing of their faith and love according to Ephesians 1:15?
options: He gives thanks and prays for them
questions.correctAnswer: He gives thanks and prays for them
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:15 states, 'Wherefore I also, after I heard of your faith... cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,' indicating his response.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 1:16 emphasize about Paul's attitude toward the Ephesians?
options: He does not care about them
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:16 emphasizes that Paul 'Cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,' reflecting his continual prayer for them.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 1:10 indicate about the fullness of times?
options: It is a time of judgment
It is when all things will be gathered together in Christ
It is a time of chaos
It is a time of peace
questions.correctAnswer: It is when all things will be gathered together in Christ
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:10 states, 'That in the dispensation of the fulness of times he might gather together in one all things in Christ...' confirming the correct answer.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 1:7 say we have through His blood?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:7 states, 'In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins...' which supports the correct answer.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 1:6, why are we accepted in the beloved?
options: By the glory of His grace
questions.correctAnswer: By the glory of His grace
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:6 states, 'To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved,' indicating the reason for our acceptance.

questions.question: What does Ephesians 1:5 highlight about our adoption?
options: It is based on our merits
It is predestinated according to His will
It is limited to certain people
questions.correctAnswer: It is predestinated according to His will
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:5 states, 'Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,' confirming the correct answer.

questions.question: The statement 'We have obtained an inheritance' is found in which verse?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:11 clearly states, 'In whom also we have obtained an inheritance...' confirming the correct verse.

questions.question: Is it true that Paul encourages prayer for the Ephesians in Ephesians 1:16?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:16 states, 'Cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers,' affirming the truth of the statement.

questions.question: Is it false that we are predestinated according to our works, as stated in Ephesians 1:11?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:11 indicates that we are predestinated 'according to the purpose of him who worketh all things...' rather than our works, making the statement false.

questions.question: Is it false that the holy Spirit is described as the earnest of our inheritance in Ephesians 1:14?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:14 states, 'Which is the earnest of our inheritance...' confirming that the statement is false.

hard.title: Ephesians Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ephesians Chapter 1.

questions.question: What does Paul pray for in Ephesians 1:17?
options: The spirit of wisdom and revelation
questions.correctAnswer: The spirit of wisdom and revelation
questions.explanation: Paul prays for 'the spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of him' as stated in Ephesians 1:17.

questions.question: What is the hope of his calling mentioned in Ephesians 1:18?
questions.explanation: The hope of his calling refers to the expectation of eternal life, as indicated in Ephesians 1:18.

questions.question: According to Ephesians 1:19, what is the exceeding greatness of his power directed towards?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:19 states that the greatness of His power is directed towards 'us-ward who believe.'

questions.question: What did God do in Christ according to Ephesians 1:20?
options: He raised him from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: He raised him from the dead
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:20 explains that God raised Christ from the dead, highlighting His divine power.

questions.question: Ephesians 1:21 states that Christ is far above all principality and power. What does this signify?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:21 indicates that Christ is 'far above all principality, and power, and might,' signifying His authority over spiritual beings.

questions.question: In Ephesians 1:22, who is given to be the head over all things to the church?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:22 states that God gave Christ to be the head over all things to the church.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'apocalypsis' mean in Ephesians 1:17?
questions.explanation: 'Apocalypsis' means 'revelation,' which is relevant in Ephesians 1:17 where Paul seeks wisdom and revelation.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Ephesians 1:18 with the phrase 'the eyes of your understanding being enlightened'?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the eyes of your understanding being enlightened' uses metaphor to express gaining insight and knowledge.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with the theme of 'inheritance' found in Ephesians 1:11?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 32:9 discusses the Lord's portion as His people, connecting to the theme of inheritance in Ephesians 1:11.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the idea of being sealed with the Holy Spirit as mentioned in Ephesians 1:13?
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 1:22 mentions being sealed by the Holy Spirit, echoing the idea found in Ephesians 1:13.

questions.question: What comes before Ephesians 1:17?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:16 comes directly before Ephesians 1:17, where Paul mentions giving thanks for the Ephesians.

questions.question: Ephesians 1:23 refers to the church as Christ's body. What does this signify in terms of unity?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:23 signifies unity, indicating that the church is the body of Christ, which is one and whole.

questions.question: The term 'predestinated' in Ephesians 1:5 implies what about God's plan?
questions.explanation: The term 'predestinated' indicates that God's plan for adoption was predetermined, as stated in Ephesians 1:5.

questions.question: True or False: Ephesians 1:12 states that we should be to the praise of His glory.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:12 states that 'we should be to the praise of his glory', confirming the statement as true.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'the fulness of him that filleth all in all' in Ephesians 1:23 refers to the church's independence.
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:23 describes the church as the body of Christ, emphasizing dependence and unity, making the statement false.

theological.title: Ephesians Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ephesians Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ephesians 1:4 teach about God's nature in election?
options: God chose believers before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless
God’s election depends on human merit and works
Election is based on foreseen faith and repentance
God’s choice is conditional upon obedience after salvation
questions.correctAnswer: God chose believers before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:4 states that God 'hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love,' teaching unconditional election based on God's sovereign will.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning redemption is taught in Ephesians 1:7?
options: Redemption and forgiveness of sins are obtained through Christ’s blood according to the riches of grace
Redemption is earned by fulfilling the law perfectly
Redemption is a future event only applicable after judgment
Forgiveness is contingent on continual human effort
questions.correctAnswer: Redemption and forgiveness of sins are obtained through Christ’s blood according to the riches of grace
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:7 teaches that 'in whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace,' emphasizing the sufficiency of Christ’s atoning blood for salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ephesians 1:13 teach about the role of the Holy Spirit in salvation?
options: Believers are sealed with the Holy Spirit as a guarantee of their inheritance
The Holy Spirit is only given after a lifetime of good works
The Spirit’s sealing can be lost through sin
The Holy Spirit’s role is symbolic with no practical effect
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are sealed with the Holy Spirit as a guarantee of their inheritance
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:13 states believers 'were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,' indicating the Spirit’s role as a divine seal and guarantee of the believer’s inheritance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ephesians 1:11 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:11 speaks of God 'who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will,' demonstrating God’s sovereign control over all things.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Ephesians 1:8?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:8 notes God 'hath abounded toward us in all wisdom and prudence,' emphasizing divine wisdom in dispensing grace.

questions.question: How does Ephesians 1:3 connect to the overall biblical theme of spiritual blessings?
options: It unfolds the concept of spiritual blessings being given in heavenly places through Christ
It confines blessings to earthly prosperity and success
It denies any blessings beyond material gifts
It teaches blessings are earned by human achievement
questions.correctAnswer: It unfolds the concept of spiritual blessings being given in heavenly places through Christ
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:3 blesses God for 'all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ,' connecting to biblical themes of blessings as divine gifts beyond material or earthly measures.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made in Ephesians 1:20 regarding Christ’s resurrection?
options: Christ’s resurrection and exaltation to the right hand of God fulfills Psalm 110:1 and Daniel's messianic expectations
The resurrection is a minor event with no theological significance
Christ remains in the grave awaiting final judgment
His resurrection is limited to a spiritual metaphor only
questions.correctAnswer: Christ’s resurrection and exaltation to the right hand of God fulfills Psalm 110:1 and Daniel's messianic expectations
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:20 describes God raising Christ and seating Him at His right hand, fulfilling Old Testament messianic prophecies such as Psalm 110:1 about the exalted Messiah.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Ephesians 1:5 and Ephesians 1:11 teach about God's will and predestination?
options: God predestinated believers according to His good pleasure and works all things according to His counsel
Predestination is a human decision based on foreseen merit
God’s predestination is arbitrary and without purpose
Believers have ultimate control over predestination
questions.correctAnswer: God predestinated believers according to His good pleasure and works all things according to His counsel
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:5 states predestination is 'according to the good pleasure of his will,' while 1:11 affirms God 'worketh all things after the counsel of his own will,' together teaching God’s sovereign and purposeful election.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ephesians 1:13 and Ephesians 1:14 teach about the Holy Spirit's role in the believer’s inheritance?
options: The Spirit seals believers as a guarantee (earnest) of the full redemption to come
The Spirit’s presence is temporary and conditional
Believers must earn the Spirit’s seal by works
The Spirit’s role is only to convict unbelievers
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit seals believers as a guarantee (earnest) of the full redemption to come
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:13 mentions believers 'were sealed with that holy Spirit,' and 1:14 calls the Spirit 'the earnest of our inheritance,' together teaching the Spirit as a divine pledge of final redemption.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ephesians 1:17 and Ephesians 1:18 teach about divine revelation and understanding?
options: God grants believers the Spirit of wisdom and revelation to enlighten their understanding of hope and inheritance
Spiritual knowledge comes only through human reason apart from God
Faith does not require understanding or enlightenment
God withholds wisdom and revelation for His glory alone
questions.correctAnswer: God grants believers the Spirit of wisdom and revelation to enlighten their understanding of hope and inheritance
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:17 prays for the Spirit of wisdom and revelation, and 1:18 speaks of enlightened understanding regarding hope and inheritance, indicating divine empowerment for spiritual insight.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Ephesians 1:5–6 promotes fatalism by teaching predestination. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches God's gracious and purposeful predestination to adoption, highlighting His good pleasure, not fatalism
It claims human free will is the sole cause of salvation
It denies any divine involvement in salvation
It teaches predestination is random and without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches God's gracious and purposeful predestination to adoption, highlighting His good pleasure, not fatalism
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:5–6 states God 'predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,' emphasizing gracious divine purpose rather than fatalistic determinism.

questions.question: What doctrine about the church is taught in Ephesians 1:22–23 regarding Christ’s relationship to it?
options: The church is the body of Christ, filled with His fullness and under His headship
The church is a separate institution unrelated to Christ
Christ is only a symbolic figurehead with no real authority over the church
The church’s fullness is independent of Christ
questions.correctAnswer: The church is the body of Christ, filled with His fullness and under His headship
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:22–23 teaches Christ is 'head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all,' defining the church as His living body under His sovereign rule.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Ephesians 1:9 regarding God's will?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:9 states God 'hath purposed in himself' His will, showing His sovereign authority to reveal and accomplish His divine plan.

questions.question: What theological synthesis is found in Ephesians 1:12 and 1:16 concerning faith, love, and prayer?
options: Believers' faith and love motivate continual intercessory prayer for them
Faith and love exclude the need for prayer
Prayer is only for personal needs, not for others
Love has no role in the Christian community
questions.correctAnswer: Believers' faith and love motivate continual intercessory prayer for them
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:12 mentions 'who first trusted in Christ,' and 1:16 shows Paul ceases not to give thanks and pray for them due to their faith and love, linking faith, love, and prayer.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical significance does Ephesians 1:10 reveal about Christ's cosmic role?
options: Christ will gather all things in heaven and earth in the fullness of times, fulfilling God’s redemptive plan
Christ’s role is limited to earthly ministry only
Redemption applies only to Israel, not all creation
The cosmic gathering is a myth with no biblical basis
questions.correctAnswer: Christ will gather all things in heaven and earth in the fullness of times, fulfilling God’s redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Ephesians 1:10 speaks of God’s plan 'to gather together in one all things in Christ,' connecting to the biblical theme of cosmic reconciliation and restoration.
